transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with constant, uncontrollable worry about almost every area of my life for about a year and a half now. It happens nearly every day, and I just can't seem to stop it.

Are these worries mostly about everyday life concerns like work, health, or family, or do you experience repetitive, intrusive thoughts that make you feel driven to perform certain actions or rituals to quiet them?

They are definitely about everyday things like my job, my family, and our finances. I don't feel any urge to perform rituals or physical actions to quiet them. The thoughts just intrude and are really hard to stop, but they are always focused on those daily life concerns.
Alongside this constant worry, have you also been experiencing a persistently low or sad mood, or a loss of interest and pleasure in the things you normally enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel persistently sad or have lost interest in the things I normally enjoy. My main struggle is really just this constant, uncontrollable worry that keeps my mind racing all the time.
Along with this constant worry, do you often experience physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, feeling easily fatigued, irritability, or trouble sleeping?

No, I haven't really noticed or experienced those kinds of physical symptoms. For me, it is really just the constant mental loop of worrying, rather than feeling physically tense, tired, or having trouble sleeping.
How does this constant worry affect your daily life, such as your ability to work, socialize, or manage your relationships and responsibilities?

It makes it extremely difficult to focus on my daily tasks because these anxious thoughts suddenly intrude and disrupt my concentration. Since this worry spreads across so many areas like my work, family, and finances, I struggle to manage my day-to-day responsibilities effectively.
Have you struggled with focus, organization, or forgetfulness since childhood, or did these concentration difficulties only start when your worries began a year and a half ago?

No, I didn't struggle with focus or organization during childhood at all; these concentration difficulties only started about a year and seven months ago when my worries began. Now, my focus issues only happen because anxious thoughts suddenly intrude into my mind and disrupt my attention while I'm trying to get things done.
Have you recently been diagnosed with any medical conditions, like thyroid issues, or do you use substances or caffeine that might be contributing to this constant worry?
No, I haven't been diagnosed with any medical conditions like thyroid issues recently. I also don't use any substances, and I don't drink much caffeine at all.
Do you ever experience sudden, unexpected surges of intense fear or discomfort that peak within minutes, commonly known as panic attacks?
No, I don't experience those sudden, intense surges of fear or panic attacks. For me, it is more of a constant, lingering state of worry that is always there in the background.
Did these worries start after a specific, major life change or stressful event about a year and a half ago, or did they seem to develop on their own?
I'm not really sure if there was a specific stressful event that triggered it. The worries just seemed to develop gradually on their own, starting about a year and seven months ago.
Do you find that your worries are mostly triggered by social situations, like speaking in public or meeting new people, because you're afraid of being judged or embarrassed?

No, my worries aren't really triggered by social situations or a fear of being judged by others. Instead, I find myself constantly worrying about a wide variety of everyday things, like my work, my family, and our finances. It is much more general than just being in social settings.
